uncited: This approach solves the coverage gaps and geometric distortions inherent in single-view projection methods, which fail when surface normals are perpendicular to the view direction [3482-single-2d-projection-voxelization.md].

The family relies on the principle that projecting a 3D object from multiple orthogonal directions ensures that every surface element is visible from at least one viewpoint, preventing "shadow" voxels caused by occlusion or grazing angles [3892-orthographic-multi-view-voxelization.md].
Alternatively, intermediate 2D buffers (sheets) are synthesized into a final 3D representation [3892-orthographic-multi-view-voxelization.md].

These cases are handled by either skipping the view for that triangle, expanding the triangle, or rasterizing along a different axis where the projection area is non-zero [3892-orthographic-multi-view-voxelization.md].
